codelines.evidence: Searched for confirmEmail/checkout email references and found src/components/pages/CheckoutPage/CheckoutForm.tsx, which renders the 'email' and 'confirmEmail' FormInput fields. The confirmEmail field's validate rule (line 305-309) does `if (email && value && value !== email) { return t("TRM774"); }` — a case-sensitive strict string comparison, exactly matching the ticket's description of the Go-Checkout page flagging same-email-different-casing as a mismatch. TRM774 is the dictionary term referenced in one of the linked ticket documents. Also opened types.ts confirming ICheckoutFormValues has email/confirmEmail as plain strings, and CheckoutForm.spec.tsx which has an existing test 'should trigger validation error on blur only when confirmEmail field is not empty' exercising this validation path with getEmail()/getConfirmEmail() helpers.

recommendedInvestigators.focus: Confirm whether any other email-comparison logic exists beyond CheckoutForm.tsx (e.g. server-side/API validation of email/confirmEmail on submit) that would also need case-insensitive treatment, and check EMAIL_REGEX/EMAIL_INPUT_MAX_LENGTH constants for any casing-related assumptions.
recommendedInvestigators.why: The bug site found in CheckoutForm.tsx is a client-side react-hook-form validate rule; there may be additional validation (e.g. in an API route or shared checkout schema) that duplicates this comparison and was not fully surveyed.

recommendedWriters.focus: Change the confirmEmail validate rule's equality check in CheckoutForm.tsx to compare emails case-insensitively (e.g. normalize casing before comparing), and update/add test coverage in CheckoutForm.spec.tsx for mixed-case matching emails passing validation and genuinely different emails still failing.
recommendedWriters.why: CheckoutForm.tsx:306 contains the exact strict `value !== email` comparison causing the reported case-sensitivity bug, and CheckoutForm.spec.tsx already has an existing test suite structure for this validation path that a fix should extend.
